appraisal_events.evidence: vous ne savez même pas sur quoi vous vous asseyez... puisque j'étais tout et que vous n'étiez rien, c'est moi qui ai fait les premiers pas vers vous... cela a eu pour effet de vous en faire faire deux cents en arrière. Maintenant c'est à moi de m'éloigner et nous ne nous connaîtrons plus.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus sustains a long, dominating tirade mocking the narrator's ignorance and unworthiness, casting himself as a wounded benefactor, and unilaterally declaring the end of their acquaintance.

appraisal_events.evidence: on ne pouvait nier que la sienne, par un vaste écart de compas, avait vue sur beaucoup de choses qui resteraient toujours inconnues au duc de Guermantes... n'en était pas moins supérieur de cent coudées à son frère, sa belle-sœur, etc.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's own aside credits Charlus's intelligence as vastly surpassing his brother's and sister-in-law's, even while noting Charlus's repellent, dangerous character, producing a mixed but locally elevating comparative judgment.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator remains passive and dominated throughout, mocked and ultimately cast off, unable to mount an effective defense.
Charlus controls the entire exchange with an elaborate, unchallenged rhetorical performance of accusation and wounded superiority.
Charlus explicitly declares the relationship over ('nous ne nous connaîtrons plus'), formally excluding the narrator from his acquaintance.
The narrator credits Charlus with an intelligence surpassing his own relatives, a locally positive though qualified judgment.
He is explicitly named as intellectually surpassed by his brother Charlus.
As Charlus's sister-in-law, she is likewise named as intellectually surpassed by him.

ambiguities: Charlus's praised intelligence is immediately qualified by the narrator's description of him as physically repellent and capable of murderous logic, so the elevation in E2 is not unequivocal.
